Superior Court of Kern | KERN COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT

Address: 415 Truxtun Ave, Bakersfield, CA 93301

Phone: N/A

The superior court of Kern county is a city courthouse in Kern County. The building was completed and established in 1952. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. Remote Court Hearing and Interpreter services are also available. This county court provides online services like e-file, online payment, transcript requests, online payment, and many more, so it is not mandatory to go to court for these types of services. How can case information be searched?

Superior Court of Kern county case search can be found on site online using the court site online case information service. Information can be searched on the county Superior Court portal of county of kern if registered. If you are not a registered user, you can search using the case number, defendant Name, or the Hearing Date. The KCSC portal allows registered users to search for state information using the following:

  • Search by Business Name
  • Search by Case Number
  • Search by Filed Date
  • Search by Party Name

Using that portal, you can also see today's hearing or your hearing date.

How can I make a payment?

Superior Court of Kern county fines and traffic tickets payments can be made in the following ways:

· In-Person:

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card pay at the counter window. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges pay will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

· Online:

Online traffic tickets or other fines can be made using the Kern Superior Court of California Self-Service Payment Portal https://www.officialpayments.com/pc_entry_cobrand.jsp?productId=370838958768749640404564048501012665.Enter the Ticket/Citation, docket or reference number. Your case with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online. The service fees will be applied in this state. Instalments regarding payment options are also available. You can also apply for traffic school or an extension in payment for traffic ticket citations only.

· Mail:

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; 1415 Truxtun Ave, Bakersfield, CA 93301, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail by supervisors; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

How to appear remotely?

Superior Court of County of Kern and Superior Court of California remote appearances for some eligible are possible using telephone and video conferencing in the zoom application. In-person hearing is now started by supervisors, but if some members want audio or video live to stream and review, then the person has to submit the local form of KRN SUP CRT MI-0315 five days before the hearing. The judicial officer will respond to your request. If your request is accepted, you can join the stream and review via the zoom application in a video conference, and the phone number will be given to you in the audio case by supervisors. Make sure your internet connection is strong. Mute your microphone and speak only when courthouse calls your name. It is recommended to avoid running unnecessary applications when you are in the hearing. Wear a proper dress and sit where your face is visible. Recording for the case hearing is not allowed. Recording for the case hearing is strictly not allowed.

Which types of cases do the Delano division deal with?

Superior Court of County of Kern and Superior Court of California– Delano division deals with criminal, traffic, family, and small claims cases. You can bring these types of cases there for a solution. The working hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm from Monday to Thursday and 8:00 am to 12:00 pm on Friday.

Superior Court of County of Kern and Superior Court of California- Lamont deals with the civil cases in that county. The ADR is a resolution offered by this county superior court, which is very helpful in civil cases. It is a way to solve candidates dispute cases with any court trial or without going to review. This resolution gives many alternative resolution processes to the lawsuit and includes meditation, Dispute Resolution Program Act, Arbitration, and many more point.

How can a divorce case be filed?

Superior Court of County of Kern and Superior Court of California- Family Division handles the divorce case. You can file a divorce case even if your spouse does not agree to it, and it is only filled if you have been in county of kern for the past three months and your spouse must also be in county of kern for the last 6 months. You can come and fill in all the information and submit some documents to the court clerk's office. The fee in dollars for divorce cases is from $435 to $450.You can apply for a fee waiver if you cannot afford the fees. Visit the Self-Help Guide of California Court as references https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/divorce-california.

How to deal with traffic tickets?

Superior Court of county of kern and Superior Court of California- Metropolitan Traffic Division, Shafter, Lamont, Mojave, Ridgecrest, and Delano deal with all the matters related to traffic tickets. If you receive a traffic ticket indicating a mandatory appearance from any of these courthouse, you must appear in court on the citation date. Still, if the ticket does not indicate a mandatory appearance, then three options are available that are:

  • Pay the traffic ticket fine online, by mail, or by visiting the court front counter
  • Attend the Traffic School if your violation is eligible for this school
  • Appear in the court if you want to deal directly with the courthouse

Superior Court of county of kern and Superior Court of California- Metropolitan Traffic Division allows a person to come to the court clerk's office before the schedule if they want to appear in court.

How can small claim cases be filled?

County of kern small claims court handles all the matters in which a person sues another person for money and personal damage within the limit of $10,000. For businesses, the limit is $5000. The cases can be resolved in quick, informal, and inexpensive ways. You can take advice from a lawyer or attorney in these cases, but the lawyer or attorney is not allowed during the hearing. Rules followed in these cases are very simple, and the hearing is informal. The case can be filled out by filling out the form available at the clerk's office, online using e-filling, mailing the form at the court, or using the file at home small claims option. Fill in your and the defendant's personal information, references and reviews, the reason for your claim, and the amount you are suing. The cases can only be filled if the plaintiff's age is 18+; otherwise, the guardian must come with the minor. After the claim is filed, the court clerk will mail the defendant about the case and the schedule. The fees depend upon the amount of money you are claiming. The fee schedule contains all the information about the court fees. The court also allows community mediation in which the trained mediators will design a program to work for both parties. They try to resolve the disputes before the filing of the case. It is a good idea to try that program without cost before filing the case in each state.

Understanding the California Court System

The California court system is divided into two main categories: trial courthouse and appellate courthouse.

Trial Courts

Trial courthouse are where cases are first heard and decided. California has two types of trial courthouse: the Superior Court and the Small Claims Court.

Superior Court

The Superior Court of California is the primary trial court. It has jurisdiction over all types of cases, including license, criminal, family law, and probate cases. The Superior Court is divided into different departments, each of which is responsible for hearing specific types of cases.

Small Claims Court

The Small Claims Court is a division of the Superior Court that is designed to handle small claims cases. These are cases where the amount of money at issue in dollars is $10,000 or less.

Appellate Courts

Appellate courthouse are responsible for reviewing decisions made by trial courthouse. California has two types of appellate courthouse: the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court.

Court of Appeal

The Court of Appeal is divided into six districts, each of which is responsible for reviewing decisions made by the Superior Court of California or County Superior courthouse within its district. The Court of Appeal has the power to uphold, modify, or reverse decisions made by the trial courthouse.

Supreme Court

The Supreme Court is the highest court in Superior Court of California. It has the power to review decisions made by the Court of Appeal and to hear cases that have statewide significance. The Supreme Court can also review decisions made by the trial courthouse if they involve important legal questions.

Jurisdiction of the Superior Court of Kern

The Superior Court of Kern along with Superior Court of California has jurisdiction over all license and criminal cases that are filed in Kern County superior. This includes cases involving:

  • Personal injury
  • Contract disputes
  • Real estate disputes
  • Criminal offenses
  • Family law matters, such as divorce and child custody
  • Probate matters, such as wills and estates

Types of Cases Heard in the Superior Court of Kern

The Superior Court of Kern hears and review a wide volume of people matters and experience way of long building things to find and provide solutions. Some of the most common types of cases heard in the Superior Court of Kern | Superior Court of California include:

A. Civil Cases

Civil cases are disputes between people individuals or organizations that do not come to point and involve criminal charges. These can include contract disputes, personal injury claims, and real estate disputes. In civil cases, the plaintiff (the person or organization bringing the lawsuit) must prove their case by a preponderance of the evidence, which means that it is more likely than not that their version of events is true.

B. Criminal Cases

Criminal cases are cases where an individual is charged with a crime, such as theft, assault, or drug possession. For people experience, the prosecution must prove their case beyond a reasonable way. If the defendant is found guilty, they may face penalties such as account fines, probation, or imprisonment.

C. Family Law Cases

Family law cases involve legal issues related to families, such as divorce, child custody, and child support. These cases can be emotional and complex, and it is important to have an experienced attorney on your side to help you navigate the process in better way.

D. Probate Cases

Probate cases involve the distribution of a deceased person's assets and the settlement of their debts. These experience can also be complex, and it is important to have an attorney who is familiar with the probate process to help you through it.

To file a case in the Superior Court of Kern or Superior Court of California, you will need to fill out the appropriate forms and pay a filing fee. You may also need to provide other documentation, depending on the type of case you are filing. Once you have filed your case, you will receive a case number and a court date with filing deadline.

Court procedures can vary depending on the type of case and the department that is hearing your case. It is important to familiarize yourself with the procedures and rules of the court to avoid any unnecessary delays or complications along with filing deadline.

Appearing in Court

If you are required to appear in court, it is important to dress appropriately and arrive on time. You should also be prepared to present your case and answer any questions that the courthouse may have.

FAQ:

What are the requirements for night court traffic?

Traffic night court requirements are:

  • You are busy during the day and cannot take day court.
  • Sign up at 4:00 pm, not later than that with the traffic division.
  • Appear for only one citation if you have many citations.

When you came for the night court, you had to bring your citation or notice of courtesy.

How can I ask for special accommodation?

You can ask for special accommodation if you have any disability or hearing impairment. You had to contact the court before the hearing date so that the court would assist you.

Can I book my case appointment online?

You can book case appointments online but only for the family law division using https://bookus.page/. Other divisions are currently not providing this facility.

I got fines from a different division; how can I pay them with only one link?

Contact the revenue recovery division, and they will give you a payment plan with the total fine from a different division, and then you can pay all fines with one link.

How can I see if my case is filled or not?

You can check if your case is filled or not by three methods:

  • Online by using smart search
  • Visit that division where your case is filled
  • Mail a request for information to the court
How to view the lep plan?

Lep Plan is a Limited English Proficiency Plan Information that can be viewed by clicking on this button https://www.kern.courts.ca.gov/.

How do I find an attorney to represent me in the Superior Court of Kern or superior court of California?

You can search for attorneys online or ask for recommendations from friends or family members. It is important to find an attorney who has experience in the type of case you are filing.

What is the difference between civil and criminal cases?

Civil volume are disputes between individuals or organizations that do not involve criminal charges. Criminal cases, on the other hand, involve charges of illegal activity, such as theft or assault.
